title: NV-DL-ADM-01..05 refuse by default with overrideChannel recordedInChain
description: The rcf-lite ruleset (`packages/rcf-lite/src/ruleset/ruleset.json`) gains five admissibility rules in the NV-DL (DefineLite) namespace: NV-DL-ADM-01 (bundle refuses without a freeze), NV-DL-ADM-02 (D4 stories floor is a finding), NV-DL-ADM-03 (D3 shapes bite is a finding), NV-DL-ADM-04 (validate finding set is a finding), and NV-DL-ADM-05 (bundle skips impacted FBS). All five carry `refuseByDefault: true` and `overrideChannel: recordedInChain`. 0.30.0 PR 8 (DEFINE step 3 spec section 4 NV-DL row, section 11.7 US-17902 appended paragraph): NV-DL-ADM-01..05 flip to `refuseByDefault`; ADM-01 and ADM-05 are the bundle refusal and skip; ADM-02..04 are D4 and D3 findings surfaced through the admissibility wrap; `overrideChannel: recordedInChain` is satisfied by `freeze.override` or an `--ack` reason. The admissibility wrap (`src/query/refuse-on-admissibility.js` plus the admissibility enforcer the chain-admissibility layer reads) surfaces ADM-02..04 as D4 and D3 findings; ADM-01 and ADM-05 are the bundle refusal and skip. readiness compute still runs and prints under refusal (0.29.0 informational posture unchanged for the compute). PR 9 enforcement locus (REQ-179 extension, spec section 17; ruling R12 2026-10-03): NV-DL-ADM-02 (D4 stories floor failing) and NV-DL-ADM-03 (D3 shapes bite failing) are surfaced through the admissibility wrap (`src/query/refuse-on-admissibility.js`, `evaluateDefineStageAdmissibility`), cited in the wrap's refusal envelope with their rule ids. For NV-DL-ADM-03 (D3 is ackable per decision 9) an `--ack <gate>=<reason>` recorded on freeze.gates at the current tree hash satisfies the recordedInChain override channel. For NV-DL-ADM-02 (D4 is NOT ackable; decision 9 keeps ackable to D3/D5/D6) the only recordedInChain override channel is `freeze.override` written by `rcf build bundle --next --override "<reason>"`; the normal path is to fix the failing D4 findings. NV-DL-ADM-04 (`rcf define validate` finding set) is surfaced through the wrap when callers pass `defineValidateErrors`; its override channel is a chain-document correction committed to git (per the ruleset note), not a gate ack. Readiness itself stays informational (AC-17902-4 unchanged); freeze keeps its own freezeableAfterAck gate.
rationale: Spec section 4 pins the NV-DL row to the ratified pattern of ruling-sheet item 1: an admissibility rule refuses by default and the override is recorded in the chain. 0.29.0 shipped the DEFINE compute and the CLI in an informational posture while PRs 5 to 7 built the biting checks; PR 8 flips the ruleset so the gate matches the checks' intent. The two override channels are the already-shipped `freeze.override` object (bundle --override) and the already-shipped `--ack` reasons recorded in freeze.gates (readiness / freeze), both of which land in the chain as part of the freeze record. Keeping readiness compute unchanged under refusal (AC-17902-4) matches ADR-4123 (refusal is informational on the compute; the gate surfaces it).
